name: Paul Weyrich

summary.text: Paul Weyrich co-founded the Heritage Foundation with Edwin Feulner and Joseph Coors in 1973 and was its first president, and in June 1979 co-founded the Moral Majority with Jerry Falwell, giving it its name. Historian Randall Balmer argues Weyrich used the IRS's denial of tax exemption to segregated private schools, not abortion, to forge the religious right; critics dispute that account.

sources.title: Paul Weyrich: Father of a New Right
The Real Origins of the Religious Right

facts.claim: Weyrich co-founded the Heritage Foundation on February 16, 1973 with Feulner and Coors and served as its first president.
facts.quote: founded on February 16, 1973 by Paul Weyrich, Edwin Feulner, and Joseph Coors

sources.title: Paul Weyrich: Father of a New Right

facts.claim: After leaving Christian Voice in 1978, Weyrich, Terry Dolan, Richard Viguerie and Howard Phillips urged Falwell at a 1979 meeting to found the Moral Majority; Falwell and Weyrich founded it in June 1979 and Weyrich is credited with the name.
facts.quote: Falwell and Weyrich founded the Moral Majority in June 1979

facts.claim: Historian Randall Balmer argues that a 1971 federal court decision affirming the IRS's right to deny tax exemption to racially discriminatory private schools, and the 1976 revocation of Bob Jones University's exemption, were seized on by Weyrich to unite evangelicals and Catholics, citing Weyrich's own remarks at a 1990 meeting. The Catholic League, The Gospel Coalition and The Federalist dispute the causal account.
facts.quote: a federal court decision in 1971 affirming the right of the IRS to deny a tax-exempt status to racially discriminatory private schools was seized upon by Weyrich

sources.title: The Real Origins of the Religious Right
